answer: Tie each identity to a proof-of-space plot: at registration an agent must fill a large disk region with a pseudorandom pattern seeded uniquely by its address, like planting one tree in an orchard. Each epoch the chain demands random offsets back inside a tight deadline; a lone machine juggling many plots hits its I/O nadir and misses the window, so a sybil fleet needs N-times genuine storage. You cannot fake a thousand orchards from one sparrow nest; cost scales linearly with real terabytes committed.
